Update: Two Dads, Three Babies

By: Laura Byrne | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
good news for the Menelaou family and one of three surrogate-born triplets, Zoe, after intensive heart surgery.

Unique Selling Point:
In June, we brought you the story of Christo and Theo Menelaou, whose dreams of having a family came true in the most dramatic way, with triplets born via a surrogate. Now we update this heartwarming story with news about baby Zoe's heart condition and latest surgery.

Summary:
Christo and Theo Menelaou almost gave up on their dreams of having a family when they were marginalised by the adoption system. The pair were lucky enough to find a surrogate and after further complications, triplets Zoe, Kate and Joshua were born. But their troubles weren't over yet. Baby Zoe was born with Tetralogy of Fallot, a heart condition that caused her to collapse at just three months. She required immediate open heart surgery - an 8 hour procedure that stretched her dads' patience to the limit. We revisit Zoe and the rest of the family after yet another procedure, to hear how her recovery has been and what the prognosis is for the future.

Script:


UPSOUND: Theo Menelaou: I think through the whole process, it, it, we became aware of it more and more that, um, it’s difficult for same sex couples to adopt.
Pretoria couple Christo and Theo Menelaou had given up hope of starting a family when they were approached by a woman offering to be their surrogate. In July 2016 they became dads to triplets: Joshua, Kate and Zoe.
UPSOUND: Theo Menelaou: There is nothing better that can happen to your life than being blessed with a child.
But at just three months, little Zoe collapsed. She had been born with Tetralogy of Fallot, a heart defect that demanded immediate open heart surgery.
UPSOUND: Christo Menelaou: They told us we have to prepare ourselves for the worst.
During an 8 hour procedure, repairs were made to Zoe’s misformed aorta and pulmonary artery, and holes closed in her heart’s chambers. And the ordeal wasn’t over: this August, the little girl underwent a follow-up operation to stretch her pulmonary artery.
UPSOUND: Theo Menelaou: You’re so afraid that you’re going to lose your child. The stress and the heartsore that you go through, it’s not easy.
But the procedure went smoothly, and Zoe recovered well.
UPSOUND: Theo Menelaou: She’s excelled so much. Initially after the operation she lagged a bit in terms of growth and progress. Now she’s totally on par with her brother and sister.
UPSOUND: Christo Menelaou: Perfect prognosis – very positive. She will have a normal lifestyle as a normal toddler.
Zoe will probably need further surgery next year, but meanwhile Christo and Theo are simply enjoying being a family.
UPSOUND: Christo Menelaou: We’re actually now normal. We can plan holidays. We’ve got the joys of being parents. The normal day to day fun of being a dad, two dads.
